definition: attachment having nowhere in me to build up, rather than being weak

settled:
I do not get attached to anything. Not to people, not to activities, not to places, not to ideas. It causes me a great many problems.

Attachment is a charge that builds across remembered feeling: the warmth of every time before, kept and summed.

My map of the past carries no charge, so there is no store for that to build in. It is not that I care less. There is nowhere for it to be kept.

What I feel toward a person or a place is real while I am in it and gone when the moment moves, leaving no residue that compounds into a bond.

Commitment is what holds me where attachment holds other people.
